retelling.text: Jesus warns the crowd that because of their loyalty to Him, they will be arrested and mistreated. They will be brought to places of worship, to prison, and before rulers, and each of these moments will become a chance to bear witness.
Jesus tells them not to spend their energy rehearsing a defense. He Himself will give them words and wisdom that none of their opponents will be able to answer or overturn.
Jesus says that even family and friends will turn them over to the authorities, and some will be killed. Many people will hate them simply because they belong to Him.
Yet Jesus promises that not a single hair on their heads will be lost. By staying steady and refusing to give up, they will gain true life.

reflectionTitle: Wednesday of the Thirty-fourth Week: Standing Firm in Faith
reflection: As the Church year draws to its close, today's readings look toward the end of all things. They do not ask us to be afraid. They ask us to be faithful.
In the First Reading, John sees those who stayed true to God standing beside a sea of glass, singing. Their song is not about their own strength. It praises God's great and wonderful works.
The Psalm picks up the same song: sing to the Lord, for He has done wondrous deeds. The victory belongs to God, and the whole creation is invited to rejoice in it.
Then the Gospel brings us back to the hard road that leads to that song. Jesus is honest. Following Him may bring misunderstanding, rejection, even betrayal by those closest to us.
What is surprising is what He asks us not to do. We are not told to build a perfect defense. We are told to trust that He will give us what we need when the moment comes.
That is not an excuse to be careless. It is an invitation to rely on Him more than on our own cleverness, our title or our preparation.

Even more striking is His promise: not a hair of our heads will be lost, though some may lose their lives. Jesus is speaking of a safety deeper than comfort. Nothing done to us can take away what God holds for us.
The word He leaves us with is perseverance. It is not flashy. It simply means staying the course, day after day, when the easy path is to quietly give in.

Most of us will never stand before a king or governor. But we face smaller tests. A colleague pressures us to cut a corner. A friend mocks what we believe. A family disagreement tempts us to hold a grudge.
Those who lead at work know this well. People watch how a leader behaves when the pressure is on. Honesty, fairness and calm under criticism are a quiet kind of witness.
Perseverance also shows up in ordinary service: showing up for a struggling employee, forgiving again, keeping a promise to the family at home when we are tired.
When we feel unprepared, we can pray before the meeting, the hard conversation or the difficult day, and ask Jesus for the wisdom He promised.
And we can take courage from the saints, like Saint Catherine of Alexandria, who held on to Christ under great pressure and now share in the song of the victorious.
message: Stay faithful in the small tests of today, trusting that Jesus will give you the words and the strength you need, and that nothing can take from you the life He holds for you.
